risk_register.mitigation: Nobody's Child will implement a regular data quality check on their Shopify platform to ensure that product information, including sizes, is accurate and up-to-date.

fashion_extensions_applied: Size and measurement data inconsistency across product lines prevents sizing AI from functioning reliably
Unstructured returns-reason data means Agent 2 recommendations for returns AI cannot be validated against real patterns

risk_register.label: Regulatory compliance risk
risk_register.trigger_reason: governance_compliance final_score=6.07 vs thresholds HIGH<4.0 MEDIUM<6.0
risk_register.mitigation: Nobody's Child will review and update their governance compliance policies to ensure they are aligned with the latest regulatory requirements for AI-powered marketing tools like Klaviyo.
risk_register.regulatory_ref: UK GDPR 2018 — consent, data minimisation, subject access rights
fashion_extensions_applied: Personalisation profiling requires explicit consent — not implied by purchase history alone under UK GDPR
Automated pricing decisions may require human review disclosure under the UK AI Bill 2026

risk_register.label: Staff adoption risk
risk_register.trigger_reason: staff_digital_literacy final_score=6.8 vs thresholds HIGH<4.0 MEDIUM<6.0
risk_register.mitigation: Nobody's Child will provide regular training sessions for staff on using Shopify's digital tools, focusing on improving their digital literacy and reducing the risk of adoption issues.
fashion_extensions_applied: Longer-serving retail staff may resist AI-assisted product recommendations if they perceive it as undermining their styling expertise
Owner-manager resistance is the single strongest predictor of failed AI adoption in fashion SMEs

risk_register.label: Vendor dependency risk
risk_register.mitigation: Nobody's Child will conduct a thorough review of their marketing automation tool, Klaviyo, to ensure it is properly integrated with Shopify and aligned with their business goals, reducing vendor dependency risk.
risk_register.regulatory_ref: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 — data portability provisions
fashion_extensions_applied: Shopify platform dependency — significant portions of Agent 2 recommendations assume Shopify, creating risk if the business migrates platforms
Single marketing automation vendor lock-in — if Klaviyo is the only tool, all customer communication is at risk from a single vendor decision

risk_register.label: AI accuracy and hallucination risk
risk_register.mitigation: Nobody's Child will implement a human review process for AI-generated content on their website to prevent hallucinations and ensure accuracy, particularly in product descriptions and size guidance.
risk_register.regulatory_ref: UK AI Bill 2026 — accuracy and transparency obligations
fashion_extensions_applied: AI-generated size advice that is wrong drives returns rather than reducing them — directly counterproductive to the primary use case
AI-generated product descriptions containing incorrect material composition create trading standards liability

risk_register.label: Ethical and bias risk
risk_register.mitigation: Nobody's Child will conduct an annual bias audit of their marketing automation tools, including Klaviyo, to identify and address any potential biases in AI-driven decision-making processes.
risk_register.regulatory_ref: UK Equality Act 2010 — protected characteristics in automated decision-making
fashion_extensions_applied: Sizing bias — AI sizing recommendations trained primarily on standard UK size data may underserve plus-size, petite or non-standard body types who represent a majority of real customers
Fast-fashion sustainability — AI demand forecasting optimised purely for sell-through rate may conflict with the business's sustainability commitments or consumer expectations around overconsumption

deliverables.name: shopify_integration_guide

instructions: Log in to your Shopify admin panel and navigate to "Settings" > "Apps".
Click on "Get apps or themes" and search for a returns management app that supports custom forms, such as AfterShip or ReturnLogic.
Install the chosen app and follow its setup instructions to integrate it with your Shopify store.
In the Shopify admin panel, go to "Settings" > "Policies" and click on the "Returns" tab.
Scroll down to the "Return form" section and click on the "Edit return form" button.
In the edit form modal, click on the "Add a new field" button and select "Custom form" as the field type.
Paste the provided returns reason capture form HTML code into the custom form editor.
Configure any additional settings or integrations required by your chosen returns management app.
Save the changes to the return form and test it in a simulated return scenario to ensure proper functionality.
